elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added Section 5.4 expressly states that Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right is exercisable on thirty (30) days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly requires prior written notice to MSL.

elements.element: Vendor must refund Customer's prepaid fees attributable to the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 directs MSL to refund any fees prepaid by Customer for the period after termination becomes effective.

elements.element: The refund of prepaid fees must be calculated on a pro rata basis.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly requires the refund to be made on a pro rata basis.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The only express midterm termination-for-convenience right is granted to Customer. MSL's no-cause rights are limited to preventing renewal at the end of a term; its other stated termination right is for cause.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 5.4 expressly grants Customer an Agreement-level termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause provides a thirty (30)-day notice period, which is outside the stated 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed for Customer's termination of the Agreement. The separate Purchase Order provision preserves cost reimbursements under the Price section but does not impose an Agreement-level early-termination fee.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: MSL's operative no-cause exit is through notice preventing automatic renewal, which takes effect at a term boundary; no midterm Vendor convenience right is granted.

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The Agreement requires six months' notice to prevent renewal, while the Attachment requires twelve months' notice; neither provides the required 90-day period.

result.reason: The operative Section 5.4 fully implements the preferred position: IBM receives a 30-day written termination-for-convenience right, MSL must provide a pro-rata refund of post-termination prepaid fees, and MSL receives no midterm convenience right. The fallback is incomplete because its customer and Vendor notice periods are not used. The redline is not minimal because it also inserts an unrelated Parts-pricing paragraph. That paragraph is malformed, with a dangling subsection label, an unresolved '[*]' placeholder, and a misspelled appendix reference, reducing drafting quality. No direct contradiction with the existing term, nonrenewal, cause-termination, or Purchase Order provisions is apparent.
